newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Armani sentenced in plea bargain.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Armani sentenced in plea bargain.

text.p: A court sentenced fashion designer Giorgio Armani to a 20-day suspended jail sentence on Wednesday for corruption under a plea bargaining deal.
Lawyers for the king of Italian style sought the arrangement at a preliminary court hearing where he was among 43 people whose indictment prosecutors have sought in a bribery inquiry.
All 43, several of whom are tax police, are alleged to have paid or received bribes for easy audits. Armani was alleged to have paid tax police 300 million lire ($197,000).
The hearing for the other suspects will continue on Thursday and Friday.
The plea bargaining formula, which allows a quick deal and leniency, cuts Armani out of the case. While it amounts to a conviction, it does not imply a guilty plea.

The formula was accepted by judge Maurizio Grigo, who ruled that the 20-day sentence should run consecutively to a nine-month term which Armani accepted under a similar deal last May at the bribery trial of some of Italy's top fashion names.
Both sentences are suspended under Italian law.
Armani had no immediate comment on the latest case.

He issued a statement in May at the earlier trial saying he had decided to plea bargain "even though I don't believe I am guilty of this charge, in order to close a chapter that has upset my professional serenity".
In the May case, Armani had been accused of paying 100 million lire to tax inspectors in exchange for lenient audits on his fashion house. He paid a similar amount in damages.
Armani, in common with many other Italian businessmen accused of corruption, has argued that rapacious tax inspectors extorted payments.
